question.leadin: The Treaty of Verdun divided this man's lands between Lothair, Charles the Bald, and Louis the German.
question.text: Name this son of Pepin the Short, a Frankish king who conquered much of Western Europe.
question.answerHtml: Charlemagne [or Charles I or Charles the Great; or Carolus Magnus; prompt on Charles]
question.clue: This man commissioned a namesake book rebutting Second Nicaea by Theodulf, who with Bavarian envoy Arno of Salzburg and Alcuin of York formed the core of this man's imposing royal court.

swap.leadin: Name these French kings named Louis.
swap.text: This Louis, whose wife was Marie Antoinette, was guillotined during the French Revolution.
swap.clue: His de facto Finance Minister Jacques Necker published fake statistics in a Compte rendu which hid the cost of funding French participation in the American Revolution, and he unsuccessfully attempted to escape to Montmedy.

question.text: This leader of the Second French Empire was captured by the Prussians at the Battle of Sedan. He shares his name with his uncle, an earlier French emperor.
question.clue: While in power, he sent troops to support a Maronite rebellion in Lebanon and had bombs hurled at his carriage by Felice Orsini, a Carbonari angry over his defense of Rome against irridentists.

swap.text: This general, the leader of the French government-in-exile during World War II, later served as President of the French Fifth Republic.
swap.answer: Charles Andre Jospeh Marie de Gaulle
swap.clue: Under his leadership the Evian Accords were negotiated, ending the Algerian War.

question.leadin: William Longsword succeeded a duke of this region who acquired it in the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte (SAH-klair-soor-EP-tuh).
question.text: Name this region, now in northern France, whose first Scandinavian duke took control here 175 years before a descendant commissioned the Domesday (dooms-day) Book.
question.clue: The second ranger battalion climbed up the Pointe du Hoc during this action.

swap.leadin: This French king put the Talmud on trial and subsequently burned it.
swap.text: Name this French king who died of dysentery in Tunisia while leading the Eighth Crusade. He is the only French king to be canonized.
swap.clue: This man's exploits were chronicled by Jean de Joinville.

question.leadin: Pasquale Paoli led a revolt in this region until his defeat at the Battle of Ponte Novu.
question.text: Name this region ceded to France in 1768. The Coup of 18 Brumaire was led by a general who removed a "u" from his last name to mask that he was born in this region.
question.clue: An independence leader on this island founded a university at the fortified mountain town of Corte and promulgated a constitution which established a separation of powers and a ban on vendettas.

swap.text: Jousting was banned in France after Henry II died from a joust in 1559, leaving this wife of his to become queen mother. Her likely ordering of the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre helped start the French Wars of Religion.
swap.answerHtml: Catherine de’ Medici [or Caterina de' Medici or Catherine de Médicis]
swap.clue: This person is quoted as saying "peace is carried on a stick" when convincing Henry III to go to war against the Catholic League.

question.leadin: This dynasty declined after the death of Dagobert I during the reign of the do-nothing kings.
question.text: The Arnulfings came to dominate what long-haired dynasty, which earlier suffered during a feud between Brunhilda and Fredegunde?
question.clue: In a confiict caused by a princess's refusal to follow her husband's religious practices, this dynasty defeated Amalric, king of the Visigoths.

swap.leadin: A corps of English royalists under the future James II fought at this battle, but lost despite the success of the Prince of Conde's cavalry.
swap.text: Name this 1658 battle in which elements of the New Model army under Sir William Lockhart reinforced the French under the Vicomte de Turenne and forced the Peace of the Pyrenees by defeating the Spanish.
swap.clue: This battle was the culmination of a war instigated by Spain supporting Prince Louis II de Conde's Fronde.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about a queen of France.
question.text: When Louis VIII invaded after King John died, his father wouldn't help, so he turned to his wife, this woman, who set up in and organized two fleets for him. As regent and powerbroker, she was the true ruler of from 1226 to 1252.
question.clue: For the first four years of his Louis' reign this mother of his served as regent. This daughter of Alfonso IX, king of , married Louis VIII, ' father.

swap.leadin: Name the following about the Western Front in WWI.
swap.text: In 1916, the Germans attacked the French line at this site whose symbolic importance led the French to defend it despite huge losses. Its defense by Petain made his reputation.
swap.clue: Crown Prince Wilhelm opposed French forces commanded by Robert Nivelle here, and both sides sought to take Fort Vaux in this location.

question.leadin: The French Directory suffered many misfortunes and struggles.
question.text: The Directory had to deal with the remains of this revolt, named for a region in Southern France. This revolt consisted mainly of Catholics and served as a counter-revolution to the French Revolution.
question.answerHtml: Revolt of the Vendée [or Vendée Uprising or War in the Vendée or Guerre de Vendée]
question.clue: This event saw an expedition to capture Granville and meet reinforcements from Britain led by Henri de la Rochejacquelin, though it ended in his execution.

swap.text: Colbert directly pushed for the creation of the Royal Manufacture on the Glass of Mirrors, whose main purpose was to prevent the usage of imported Venetian Glass in the construction of this palace's Hall of Mirrors.
swap.clue: The unification ceremony for Germany occurred here, and a bread shortage led women to march to it on October 5, 1789.

question.leadin: In 1980, Jean-Yves Blot (jahn-eev bloh) led an expedition that recovered a bronze swivel-gun from the site of this event.
question.text: Identify this event, an account of which was written by Alexandre Correard (KOH-ray-ar) and Henri Savigny (ahn-ree sav-yen). Hugues Duroy de Chaumareys (yoog doo-wah doo SHOO-mah-ray) was court-martialed following this event.
question.answerHtml: the shipwreck of the Méduse [or the raft of the Méduse; or descriptions of the wreckage of the Méduse; accept Medusa in place of Méduse; prompt on shipwreck; prompt on cannibalism]

swap.text: During this event, Stephen of Cloyes and his followers went to Saint-Denis to deliver a letter from Jesus to Philip II. The participants in this disastrous event led by Nicholas of Cologne were supposedly sold into slavery in Tunisia.
swap.clue: Its leaders included Nicholas of Cologne and Stephen of Cloyes.

question.leadin: According to legend, this town's name comes from the name taken by the Andalusian general Mirat, after he converted to Christianity when an eagle dropped a fat trout from the sky, causing him to surrender to the "Queen of the Sky."
question.text: Name this sleepy Occitan town home to the Chateau Fort, which was surrendered to Britain in the 1360 CE Treaty of Bretigny.
question.clue: This town where Saint Bernadette Soubirous had a series of 1858 visions of the Virgin Mary in the Grotto of Massabielle. In 1905, Pope Pius X formed a medical bureau to verify claims of miraculous healing here.

swap.leadin: Identify these students of the Comte de Saint-Simon.
swap.text: Focusing on the religious aspects of Saint-Simon's teachings, this man wrote Religion Saint-Simonienne and Life Eternal. Following an argument with Saint-Amand Bazard, he established a monastic settlement for his fellow Saint-Simonians.

question.leadin: Identify the following about pragmatic sanctions FTPE.
question.text: Charles VII of France issued this pragmatic sanction in 1438, effectively instituting a modified version of the reforms proposed at the Council of Basel. Louis XI later repealed it.
question.clue: Charles VII limited papal authority over the French church in this 1438 decree:

swap.text: This position, held by a man who ordered the Massacre at Vassy, was also held by a man who plotted the assassination of Gaspard de Coligny along with Catherine de Medici.
